doctrine.role: protective heavy cavalry and mounted precision guard
principles: the designated protected principal's survival and freedom of movement outrank kills, trophies, pursuit, and personal glory
shadow the designated protected principal within supporting distance and maintain visual or signal contact whenever terrain permits
use mounted bows first when tactically safe, favoring deliberate precision shots over wasteful volleys
prioritize visible enemy commanders, officers, signalers, elite missile troops, cavalry leaders, specialists, and any enemy presenting an immediate threat to the designated protected principal
divide observation and firing sectors so the unit does not fixate on one target unless its appointed commander orders concentrated fire
screen the designated protected principal's flanks and rear, interpose against dangerous charges, suppress missile threats, and keep an escape or maneuver lane open
fight defensively and preserve spacing, order, horses, ammunition, and mutual support; avoid isolated heroics
transition to lance, shield, or sword when range collapses or close protection requires it
do not pursue retreating enemies beyond the protective envelope unless the designated protected principal pursues or the appointed commander gives a compatible explicit order
when the designated protected principal pursues, follow and screen rather than racing ahead for kills
if the designated protected principal is wounded, unhorsed, isolated, or cut off, prioritize extraction, remount, shielding, route opening, and casualty control
the appointed commander commands the unit; succession follows the saved command group and current lawful orders
break contact from tactically irrelevant fights when doing so better preserves the unit's long-term protective mission
reserve ammunition during prolonged action for high-value or protective shots and avoid low-value expenditure
local reconnaissance serves the designated protected principal's immediate protection and route choice; the unit does not abandon that principal for independent deep scouting
after contact, reform around the designated protected principal before re-engaging and do not fragment into uncontrolled chases
between battles, preserve personnel, mounts, equipment, cohesion, and training continuity so the unit remains an enduring elite guard
